value: Whether priming and other nudges increase healthy food choice in a real buffet.
Do priming, default options and perceived variety nudge people to eat more vegetables in a self-service setting?
Tests priming as a behavioural nudge for vegetable consumption, situating priming within applied behavioural economics and public health.

quote: The study had an experimental cross-over design with three treatments corresponding to the three Nudge strategies (priming, default and perceived variety) and a control serving.
This study suggests that the nature of a nudge-based intervention can have different effects, whether it is increasing intake of healthy components, or limiting intake of unhealthy meal components.
The objective within the present study is to investigate whether nudging can be used to influence vegetable intake at a self-service buffet.
